$description: MLS Design System token source of truth. W3C Design Tokens Community Group format. Everything in dist/ is generated from this file by scripts/build.mjs -- edit here, never there.

color.$description: Three tiers. primitive = raw ramp values, no meaning. brand = the league marks. semantic = role-based, theme-aware, and the ONLY tier product code should reference.

primitive.$description: Perceptually-even ramps generated in OKLCH by scripts/gen_ramps.py. Neutrals carry a navy cast borrowed from the league navy so greys read as MLS grey rather than generic grey.

600.$description: Pinned to the league red rather than a computed step.

900.$description: Pinned to the league navy rather than a computed step.

brand.$description: The league marks. CONFIDENCE: LOW. See docs/03-color.md and docs/16-sourcing-and-confidence.md. MLS publishes no public brand colour specification; these are the most-cited third-party values and are internally coherent (485 C / 281 C is the canonical US-and-Canada flag pairing, which matches MLS's own statement that the crest colours 'pay homage to the nations MLS represents'). Verify with MLS Brand before any print, licensing or partner use.

black.$description: Not pure black. Broadcast-safe near-black that holds detail on OLED and in stadium LED.

accent.$description: THE MOST IMPORTANT IDEA IN THIS SYSTEM. The MLS crest is chromatically parasitic by design -- it was built as a template that takes on each club's colours. So accent is a slot, not a value. It defaults to the league red and is overridden wholesale by any club theme. Product code should reference accent, never brand.red.

contrast.$description: Foreground guaranteed legible on accent.base. Club themes must override this when their primary is light (Columbus gold, Sporting blue, Inter Miami pink, NYCFC skyline blue).

semantic.$description: Role-based. Every value has a light and a dark counterpart. The build emits light under :root and dark under [data-theme=dark] and prefers-color-scheme.

border-strong.$description: neutral.400 would be the prettier choice but lands at 2.31:1 on white. Input borders are UI components and need 3:1.

live.$description: Reserved for genuinely live match state. Never decorative.

font.$description: Licensed originals are named FIRST in every stack so that any machine with the real MLS fonts installed uses them, and everyone else falls back to a vetted open-source substitute. No font binaries ship in this repo -- see assets/fonts/README.md.

display.$value: "MLS Tifo Headline", "MLS Headline", "Archivo Expanded", Archivo, "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
display.$description: Headlines, scorelines, stadium and broadcast. Substitute: Archivo (SIL OFL) -- one of the few open grotesques with a true width axis, which is what MLS Tifo's Regular-to-Wide range needs.

text.$value: "MLS Tifo Standard", "MLS Standard", Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
text.$description: Body, UI, long-form. Substitute: Inter (SIL OFL) -- variable neo-grotesque with an optical-size axis, engineered for screen legibility, closest available analogue to MLS Standard.

micro.$value: "MLS Tifo Micro", "MLS Micro", Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif
micro.$description: Captions, table cells, legal, anything under 13px. MLS Tifo carries a dedicated Micro optical size; Inter's opsz axis approximates it.

numeric.$value: "MLS Tifo Headline", Archivo, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
numeric.$description: Scores, standings, clocks, stats. Always pair with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, or columns will not align.

mono.$value: "JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", "Roboto Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
mono.$description: Code, token names, IDs. Not a brand face -- utility only.

extrabold.$description: Display only. Never below 24px -- it closes up and turns to mud.

fontSize.$description: Modular scale, 1.125 through the text range and widening through display. Sports products need genuinely large numerals; 8xl and 9xl exist for scorelines and stadium screens, not for headings.

relaxed.$description: Long-form editorial. Match reports and features run long -- give them air.

widest.$description: Small all-caps only. Below 12px, caps without tracking are unreadable.

space.$description: 4px base grid. Named by step, not by t-shirt size, so the scale can grow at either end without renaming anything.

radius.$description: Deliberately tight. The crest is built from straight lines, 45-degree angles and hard corners; soft rounded rectangles fight it. Where a shape needs personality, use the notch utility (a clipped 45-degree corner) instead of a larger radius.

notch.$description: Size of the 45-degree clipped corner used by .mls-notch. Derived from 'The Corners', a named device in MLS's own 2015 partner guidelines.

chart.$description: Chart colour, derived by search rather than by hand in scripts/gen_chart_palette.mjs and validated against the six categorical checks (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD separation under simulated protanopia and deuteranopia, normal-vision floor, contrast on surface). Light and dark are DIFFERENT STEPS of the same eight hues, not a flip: no single hex clears 3:1 against both white and near-black. Assign slots in fixed order, never cycled. A ninth series folds into Other, or the chart becomes small multiples.

light.$description: Worst adjacent pair 16.2 under simulated CVD against a target of 8; normal-vision floor 26.8 against a floor of 15; all eight clear 3:1 on white.

1.$description: blue, anchored on the brand navy hue

dark.$description: Worst adjacent pair 16.3 under simulated CVD; normal-vision floor 26.5; all eight clear 3:1 on the near-black surface.

sequential.$description: Magnitude. One hue, light to dark, on the brand navy. Never a rainbow.

diverging.$description: Polarity around a baseline. Two hues plus a NEUTRAL grey midpoint. Never a hue at the midpoint.

gridline.$description: Value gridlines only. Category gridlines are off.

page.$description: Print and document geometry. Values in inches; docx-js wants DXA at 1440 per inch.

measure.$description: Target characters per line at body size on Letter with 1in margins. Above ~95 a printed line is hard to track back.

slide.$description: 16:9 widescreen geometry, in inches. pptxgenjs LAYOUT_WIDE. Note its DEFAULT is 10x5.625, not this -- set pres.layout before adding any slide or content silently lands off-canvas.

margin.$description: Content edge. Above the 0.5in floor, because league decks are shown on stage where edges get cropped.

bodyTop.$description: Where body content starts under a standard slide title.

typePrint.$description: Point sizes for Word documents. A document is read at arm's length on paper or at 100% on screen, so the scale is much tighter than the slide scale. Do not reuse slide sizes in a document or every heading shouts.

typeSlide.$description: Point sizes for PowerPoint. A slide is read from the back of a room, so the floor is high: nothing below 11pt ever goes on a slide, and body sits at 16pt. Size contrast between title and body must be large or the hierarchy disappears at distance.

heroStat.$description: The single big number on a stat slide.

office.$description: Font names written into .pptx and .docx files. Office resolves a SINGLE family name, not a CSS stack, so there is no graceful fallback: a name the viewer lacks is substituted arbitrarily and the layout shifts. Two profiles, chosen deliberately. See docs/16-presentations.md.

licensedHeading.$description: Correct inside MLS, where Tifo is installed.

safeHeading.$description: Ships with every Office install and renders true-to-width, so text-fit checks are trustworthy. Correct for anything leaving the building.

shadow.$description: Restrained. MLS's own guidelines prohibit shadows and glows on the crest; the wider system follows that instinct and leans on borders and surface steps for hierarchy instead of heavy elevation.

duration.$description: Fast. The crest's 45-degree slash is documented as representing 'the nonstop nature of our game'; motion in this system should feel driven, never languid. Nothing routine exceeds 240ms.

drive.$description: Signature curve. Accelerates hard then arrives -- the motion equivalent of the slash.

geometry.$description: Constants for the two named graphic devices from MLS's own partner guidelines: The Slash and The Corners.

slashAngle.$description: Degrees. Non-negotiable. Every diagonal in the system is 45deg or it is off-brand.

crestClearSpace.$description: Multiplier. Clear space around the crest equals 4x the 'X' measurement on all sides, per the published guidelines.

crestMinWidth.$description: Published minimum print width. Digital equivalent used in this system is 32px.
